claims.claim: The workflow preserves the A1 trigger, runner, permission, repository, credential, and shell-binding constraints while accepting dispatch_id.
First-seen dispatches are durably bound before invoking the existing PRIMARY path at most once.
Duplicate terminal dispatches replay their recorded outcome without another PRIMARY or Executor invocation.
Dispatch identity collisions and malformed identifiers fail closed without gaining path, shell, or execution authority.

Restart reconciliation can uniquely attribute post-invocation RUN state without re-invoking PRIMARY; PowerShell diagnostic assertions now normalize display whitespace while preserving semantic checks.
Active, incomplete, or ambiguous reconciliation returns a non-executing outcome without retry or state mutation.
Existing direct run, synchronization, locking, dispatch, Runtime, correction, review, and publication behavior remains unchanged.
Dispatch records remain repository-local operational state distinct from canonical engineering truth and later automation authorities.
Documentation covers stable dispatch identity and no-reexecution semantics, and the roadmap records A2 separately from later gates.
